questions.q: (a) Describe how bacteria are genetically modified to produce human insulin [4]. (b) Explain two conditions that must be controlled in an industrial fermenter [4].
questions.a: (a) restriction enzyme cuts out the insulin gene (1) and opens the plasmid (1); ligase joins gene into plasmid (1); plasmid inserted into bacteria, which make insulin (1); (b) any two with reasons: temperature, optimum for enzymes (2); pH, optimum for enzymes (2); oxygen for aerobic respiration (2); aseptic to avoid contamination (2); nutrients for growth (2)
questions.model: Teacher writes the first point: 'A restriction enzyme cuts the human insulin gene out of the DNA.'

questions.q: Evaluate biological control of greenhouse whitefly using a parasitic wasp.
questions.a: Specific, no chemical residue, self-sustaining (1, 1); but slower and may not eliminate the pest/wasp could escape (1)

questions.q: Give one risk of selective breeding.
questions.a: Reduced gene pool, so more vulnerable to new diseases or inherited defects.

questions.q: Explain why adding CO₂ to a glasshouse can increase yield.
questions.a: CO₂ is a limiting factor for photosynthesis (1); more CO₂, faster photosynthesis, more glucose for growth (1)
questions.model: What limits photosynthesis? CO₂ can. Raise it: faster photosynthesis, more sugar, more growth.
